tagline: Up the Connecticut from Massachusetts farms to the Canadian line.
intro: The byway starts among the farms of South Hadley and Hadley in Massachusetts and follows the Connecticut north, on both banks, through Vermont and New Hampshire to the Canadian border, with the Green Mountains on one side and the White Mountains on the other. It is old farm country. Hadley still has the most active farmland in the region, and Sunderland's Buttonball Tree, a sycamore, was already growing when the Constitution was signed.
Bellows Falls put the first bridge across the river in 1785. Near the top, Vermont Route 26 runs about 69 feet to the New Hampshire line, the shortest signed route in the state.

moments.title: Cornish-Windsor Covered Bridge
moments.text: In 1866 the toll was 2 cents to walk into wet Cornish and 3 cents to walk back to dry Windsor. It stayed a toll bridge until 1943.

moments.title: Orford
moments.text: In 1793 Samuel Morey showed a paddlewheel driving a steamboat on the river here. Up on The Ridge stand the Seven Swans, Federal houses built between 1773 and 1839.

moments.title: Columbia Covered Bridge
moments.text: The third bridge on the site, built in 1912 after fire took the last one, crossing 146 feet of river from Lemington to Columbia, New Hampshire.

practical: Mud season can come any time from March to May, with frost heaves and potholes on dirt and secondary roads, and towns with gas can be 10 to 30 miles apart.
